security.page.title: Security
security.page.descriptionFallback: How people sign in to this workspace.
security.mfa.title: Require two-factor authentication
security.mfa.description: Every member of this workspace signs in with a code from an authenticator app, on top of their password or social login.
security.mfa.on: On: members without 2FA set it up when they sign in, and nobody can disable it.
security.mfa.off: Off: each member decides whether to use 2FA.
security.mfa.allMembersCovered: Every active member has two-factor authentication.
security.mfa.membersWithout: {count, plural, one {# active member does} other {# active members do}} not have two-factor authentication yet.
security.mfa.membersWithoutAtLeast: At least {count, plural, one {# active member does} other {# active members do}} not have two-factor authentication yet.
security.adminOnly: Only workspace admins can change this setting.
security.mfa.ownFirst.title: Your own account needs 2FA first
security.mfa.ownFirst.description: You can only require two-factor authentication from the workspace once you have set it up yourself.
security.mfaModal.requireUnknown: Members without two-factor authentication get an email about it, and will be asked to set it up at their next sign-in, within 24 hours at most for people who are currently signed in.
security.mfaModal.requireAllCovered: Every active member already has two-factor authentication. People joining later will be asked to set it up when they sign in.
security.mfaModal.requireCount: {count, plural, one {# active member does} other {# active members do}} not have two-factor authentication yet. They get an email about it, and will be asked to set it up at their next sign-in, within 24 hours at most for people who are currently signed in.
security.mfaModal.requireCountAtLeast: At least {count, plural, one {# active member does} other {# active members do}} not have two-factor authentication yet. They get an email about it, and will be asked to set it up at their next sign-in, within 24 hours at most for people who are currently signed in.
security.mfaModal.liftDescription: Members keep the two-factor authentication they have set up, but they will be able to disable it, and new members will no longer be asked to set it up.
security.mfaModal.liftSuccess: Two-factor authentication is no longer required
security.mfaModal.error: Could not update the two-factor authentication requirement
security.ssoModal.enforceUnknown: Everyone whose address is on a verified domain of this workspace will sign in through your identity provider, and only through it.
security.ssoModal.enforceCount: {count, plural, one {# active member} other {# active members}} on your verified domains will sign in through your identity provider, and only through it.
security.ssoModal.enforceCountAtLeast: At least {count, plural, one {# active member} other {# active members}} on your verified domains will sign in through your identity provider, and only through it.
security.ssoModal.liftWorkspace: People on your verified domains will be able to sign in with a password or a social account again. Those signed in through your identity provider stay signed in.
security.ssoModal.liftBackOfficeUnknown: Everyone on this workspace's verified domains will be able to sign in with a password or a social account again. Those signed in through the identity provider stay signed in.
security.ssoModal.liftBackOfficeCount: {count, plural, one {# active member} other {# active members}} on this workspace's verified domains will be able to sign in with a password or a social account again. Those signed in through the identity provider stay signed in.
security.ssoModal.liftBackOfficeCountAtL: At least {count, plural, one {# active member} other {# active members}} on this workspace's verified domains will be able to sign in with a password or a social account again. Those signed in through the identity provider stay signed in.
security.ssoModal.liftSuccess: Single sign-on is no longer required
security.ssoModal.enforceWarning: Passwords, password resets, social sign-in and e-mail changes stop working for those addresses, and everyone currently signed in with one of them is signed out.
security.ssoModal.enforceUnaffected: Guests on other domains, service accounts and AI assistants are unaffected.
security.ssoModal.backOfficeWarning: Lift the requirement only once you have verified the requester's identity through the support procedure — a request to hand a workspace back to passwords is exactly what an attacker locked out of it would ask for.
security.ssoModal.backOfficeRecorded: The workspace's admins can require it again themselves, and the lift is recorded against your account.
security.sso.loadError: The single sign-on settings could not be loaded.
security.sso.title: Single sign-on
security.sso.upsell.description: Let your team sign in with your own identity provider — Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace or any OpenID Connect and SAML provider.
security.sso.upsell.features: Claim your e-mail domains, provision accounts at first sign-in, and make your identity provider the only way into this workspace.
security.sso.adminOnly.description: This workspace can sign its members in through its own identity provider.
security.sso.memberState.none.label: Not set up
security.sso.memberState.none.descriptio: No identity provider is connected to this workspace.
security.sso.memberState.draft.label: Being set up
security.sso.memberState.draft.descripti: An identity provider is being connected. Signing in through it is not available yet.
security.sso.memberState.tested.label: Tested
security.sso.memberState.tested.descript: The identity provider answered a test sign-in. It is not switched on for members yet.
security.sso.memberState.enabled.label: Enabled
security.sso.memberState.enabled.descrip: Members on the workspace's verified domains are signed in through the identity provider by default. Their other ways of signing in still work.
security.sso.memberState.enforced.label: Required
security.sso.memberState.enforced.descri: Members on the workspace's verified domains must sign in through the identity provider.
security.sso.status.title: Status
security.sso.status.description: Single sign-on goes live in steps, so a misconfigured provider never locks anybody out.
security.sso.steps.described.title: Identity provider described
security.sso.steps.described.empty: Fill in the identity provider card above to start.
security.sso.steps.described.draft: Saved as a draft: run a test sign-in to go on.
security.sso.steps.described.saved: Saved. Changing how your provider is trusted (issuer, client ID; for SAML the entity ID, sign-on URL, or leaving none of the certificates that were valid) sends the connection back to draft. A new client secret or an added certificate does not: run a test sign-in to check it.
security.sso.steps.tested.title: Test sign-in succeeded
security.sso.steps.tested.description: Signs you in against your provider in a new window, without signing anybody in or creating anyone.
security.sso.steps.enabled.title: Single sign-on enabled
security.sso.steps.enabled.description: Addresses on your verified domains may sign in through your provider — a password still works.
security.sso.steps.enabled.noDomain: Verify one e-mail domain first: a connection only authenticates domains you own.
security.sso.steps.enforced.title: Single sign-on required
security.sso.steps.enforced.since: Required since {date}: your provider is the only way in for your verified domains.
security.sso.steps.enforced.sinceSwitche: Required since it was switched on: your provider is the only way in for your verified domains.
security.sso.steps.enforced.description: Makes your provider the only way in for every address on your verified domains.
security.domains.added: Domain added — publish the record below, then verify
security.domains.title: Verified domains
security.domains.description: Only addresses on a domain you have proven can sign in through your identity provider. Publish the TXT record we give you with your DNS provider, then verify it.
security.domains.empty: No domain claimed yet. Single sign-on cannot be enabled until one is verified.
security.domains.keepRecord: Keep the record published: we check it every day, and a domain whose record is gone stops routing to your identity provider.
security.domains.recordMissing: The record is no longer visible. Publish it again and verify — the domain comes back on its own once we see it.
security.domains.publishRecord: Publish this record with your DNS provider, then verify. It can take a few minutes to propagate.
security.domains.record.name: Name
security.idp.protocols.oidcHint: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and most modern providers.
security.idp.protocols.samlHint: The enterprise standard, and the only way in with some providers.
security.idp.title: Identity provider
security.idp.description: The provider that authenticates your team. Register this application there, then paste what it gives you here.
security.oidc.redirectUriHint: Register this address as the redirect (callback) URI of the application on your provider's side.
security.oidc.issuerHint: The provider's issuer URL. Its OpenID configuration is read from it.
security.oidc.clientSecretSaved: Saved — type a new one to replace it
security.oidc.trustNotice: Changing the issuer or the client ID sends the connection back to draft: single sign-on is switched off and the requirement lifted until a new test sign-in succeeds. A new client secret does not: run a test sign-in to check it.
security.fileInput.tooLarge: {name} is too large for this field
security.provisioning.title: Provisioning
security.provisioning.description: What people get when they sign in through your identity provider.
security.provisioning.defaultRoleHint: Admins are always appointed by hand: single sign-on never grants that role.
security.provisioning.sessionLengthHint: After this, people authenticate with your provider again — silently while their session there is still open.
security.provisioning.jitHint: Off, only people you invited — or that your directory provisions — can sign in through the connection; nobody else is created.
security.sso.popupBlocked: Allow pop-ups for this site, then start the test again
security.saml.sources.metadataUrlHint: The quickest way: the entity ID, the sign-on URL and the certificates are read from it.
security.saml.sources.metadataXmlHint: For a provider that only lets you download its metadata.
security.saml.metadataUrlHint: Read once when you save it, then watched: a change of certificates there is reported to you, never applied on its own.
security.saml.metadataXmlHint: Read once and not stored; what it says is saved on the connection.
security.saml.idpEntityIdHint: Also called issuer. Changing it makes everyone bind to the provider again at their next sign-in.
security.saml.idpCertificateHint: The certificate your provider signs its responses with. A binary .cer is converted here.
security.saml.bindingHint: How the authentication request travels to your provider. Redirect suits every common provider.
security.saml.attributeNamesHint: Where the e-mail and the names are read in the assertion. Left empty, the names the common providers use are all tried.
security.saml.allowIdpInitiated: Allow sign-in started from the identity provider
security.saml.allowIdpInitiatedHint: Off, a response must answer a request this application made. On, a tile in your provider's dashboard works — at the price of accepting responses nobody here asked for.
security.saml.trustNotice: Changing the entity ID or the sign-on URL, typed here or read from metadata, sends the connection back to draft: single sign-on is switched off and the requirement lifted until a new test sign-in succeeds. Certificates are different: adding one keeps the status, so a rotation causes no outage, and only a change that leaves none of the previously valid certificates returns the connection to draft. The attribute names and the switch above never do.
security.sp.issueNotice: The values to register on your provider's side — entity ID, sign-on URL, metadata and our signing certificate — are issued with the connection. Get them first if your provider asks for them before it gives you anything (Microsoft Entra ID does); otherwise describe your provider below and they appear with the save.
security.sp.issue: Get the values for my provider
security.sp.title: Values for your identity provider
security.sp.description: Register these in the SAML application of your provider. The metadata document holds them all, our signing certificate included.
security.sp.certificateHint: Only for a provider that verifies signed requests and asks for the certificate itself rather than reading the metadata.
security.sp.certificateHintUntil: Only for a provider that verifies signed requests and asks for the certificate itself rather than reading the metadata. Valid until {date}.
security.certificates.expiresIn: {days, plural, one {Expires tomorrow} other {Expires in # days}}
security.certificates.metadataApplied: Applied what your provider's metadata announces
security.certificates.title: Signing certificates
security.certificates.description: What responses from your identity provider are verified with. Two can be registered at once, so a rotation costs no downtime: add the new one, let your provider switch, remove the old one.
security.certificates.metadataChanged: Your provider's metadata has been announcing other certificates than the ones registered since {date}. Nothing was applied on its own — reading them in is a change of trust.
security.certificates.empty: No certificate registered. Single sign-on cannot be used until one is.
security.certificates.inputHint: A binary .cer is converted here. RSA of 2048 bits or more, signed with SHA-256 or stronger.
security.certificates.full: Two certificates are registered, which is the most a connection holds. Remove the one your provider no longer signs with to make room for the next.
security.certificates.removeDescription: Responses signed with {label} will no longer be accepted. This is the last step of a rotation, once your provider signs with the new certificate.
security.certificates.removeLastWarning: No valid certificate would be left: the connection returns to draft, single sign-on is switched off and the requirement lifted. Register the new certificate first, then remove this one.
security.domains.removeDescription: Addresses on this domain stop signing in through your identity provider. You can claim it again later, with a new DNS record to publish.
security.domains.removeLastWarning: This is the last verified domain of an active connection: removing it switches single sign-on off and lifts the requirement. Everyone signs in with their password again.
security.switchProtocol.title: Switch this connection to {protocol}?
security.switchProtocol.description: You will describe your identity provider again, with the values {protocol} asks for.
security.switchProtocol.draftWarning: Saving the new protocol returns the connection to draft: single sign-on is switched off and the requirement lifted until a new test sign-in succeeds.
security.switchProtocol.secretDropped: The stored client secret is dropped.
security.switchProtocol.certificatesRemo: The registered signing certificates are removed.
security.switchProtocol.rebind: People who signed in through this connection are matched by their address again the next time.
